applies_why: No: the judge text labels the point UNDERDETERMINED and does not count any verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. A verse the judge says was answered is not counted.
room: 'counts as an unanswered witness' and 'counts toward a broken link' — I weighed whether these apply whenever a pressed verse is mentioned in an UNDERDETERMINED ruling, or only when the judge expressly counts a verse as unanswered or broken.
why: The judge text says the row was answered and turns on underdetermination, not on counting any verse as an unanswered witness or toward a broken link.
